roadmap.title: Core RAG Architecture
roadmap.goal: Understand the complete RAG pipeline and the role of each LangChain component.

topics.title: Core RAG Architecture
theory: RAG = Retrieve → Augment → Generate
Document Loaders ingest PDFs, S3, Notion and URLs.
Text Splitters break documents into chunks.
Embeddings convert text into vectors.
Vector Stores store and search embeddings.
Retrievers fetch relevant top-k chunks.
Prompts combine questions with retrieved context.
LLMs generate the final answer.
Output Parsers convert output into structured data.

topics.title: Document Loading, Chunking & Embeddings
theory: Document Loaders ingest source data into Document objects.
Text Splitters break large documents into manageable chunks.
RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter is commonly used for recursive chunking.
Embeddings represent text as numerical vectors.
Chunk size and overlap affect retrieval quality.
topics.code:
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter

splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=1000,
    chunk_overlap=200
)

chunks = splitter.split_documents(documents)

topics.title: Vector Stores & Retrievers
theory: Vector Stores store embeddings and support similarity search.
Common vector stores include Pinecone, FAISS and Qdrant.
Retrievers provide a standard interface for fetching relevant documents.
similarity_search() can retrieve documents based on vector similarity.
Retriever.invoke(query) executes retrieval through the Runnable interface.

roadmap.title: LangChain Abstractions & LCEL
roadmap.goal: Understand LangChain Runnable abstractions and compose RAG pipelines using LCEL.

topics.title: LangChain Abstraction Layers
theory: LangChain provides standardized interfaces for RAG components.
Retrievers implement the Runnable interface.
ChatPromptTemplate dynamically injects context and question variables.
llm.invoke() provides a unified interface across LLM providers.
Output Parsers convert raw outputs into structured JSON or Pydantic objects.
Abstraction layers allow retrieval backends and LLM providers to be replaced without rewriting business logic.

topics.title: LCEL & Runnable Composition
theory: LCEL stands for LangChain Expression Language.
LCEL uses the pipe operator | to compose Runnables.
Every Runnable can support invoke, ainvoke, stream, astream and batch.
LCEL provides composability and standardized execution.
RunnableParallel executes independent branches in parallel.
RunnablePassthrough passes input through without modification.
topics.code:
chain = (
    retriever
    | prompt
    | llm
    | parser
)

result = chain.invoke(query)

async for chunk in chain.astream(query):
    print(chunk)
hands: Build a complete RAG chain using LCEL.
Add streaming using astream().
Use RunnableParallel for independent operations.
Use RunnablePassthrough to preserve the original question.

topics.title: Runnable Execution APIs
theory: invoke() executes a Runnable synchronously.
ainvoke() executes a Runnable asynchronously.
stream() returns incremental output.
astream() provides asynchronous streaming.
batch() executes multiple inputs.
Streaming improves perceived time-to-first-token.

stream vs astream?

roadmap.title: Production RAG & Framework Tradeoffs
roadmap.goal: Understand production limitations and decide when to use LangChain versus custom SDK implementations.

topics.title: Production Scale Limitations
theory: LangChain is useful for rapid prototyping and integrations.
Wrapper objects can introduce additional latency.
Rapid API changes can create long-term maintenance challenges.
Deep abstraction layers can make debugging harder.
Large dependency footprints can increase application complexity.
Framework constraints can reduce low-level control.
topics.code:
Prototype
   ↓
LangChain
   ↓
Production Hot Path
   ↓
Measure Latency
   ↓
Use Custom Code Where Necessary

topics.title: LangChain vs Custom SDK
theory: LangChain provides fast development and standardized integrations.
Custom SDK implementations provide maximum control.
Direct SDK calls can provide more precise token control.
Custom pipelines can be useful for highly customized retrieval logic.
Latency-sensitive hot paths may benefit from reduced framework abstraction.
The decision depends on productivity, performance, stability and control requirements.

retriever | prompt | llm | parser

Custom SDK:

  ↓

  ↓
llm_client.generate()

parse_response()

roadmap.title: Multi-Step & Conversational RAG
roadmap.goal: Build RAG systems that can decompose complex questions and maintain conversational context.

topics.title: Multi-Step & Multi-Hop RAG
theory: Multi-step reasoning decomposes complex questions into sub-questions.
Each sub-question can execute a separate retrieval operation.
Retrieved chunks can be deduplicated before synthesis.
The final LLM combines retrieved evidence into a cohesive answer.
Modern implementations commonly use LCEL and LangGraph instead of subclassing legacy Chain.
topics.code:
sub_questions = llm.invoke(question)

docs = [
    retriever.invoke(q)
    for q in sub_questions
]

answer = llm.invoke(
    synthesis_prompt(docs)
)

Retrieve documents for multiple sub-questions.

topics.title: Conversational RAG & Memory
theory: Conversational RAG maintains context across user turns.
Follow-up questions may need query reformulation before retrieval.
Buffer Memory keeps the full conversation history.
Window Memory keeps the last K turns.
Summary Memory summarizes older conversation history.
Production systems should persist history in external stores such as Redis or PostgreSQL.

roadmap.title: Streaming & Hybrid Retrieval
roadmap.goal: Implement production-friendly streaming and improve retrieval using hybrid search and reranking.

topics.title: Streaming Responses
theory: Streaming sends generated tokens progressively to the client.
Streaming improves perceived time-to-first-token latency.
Retrieval generally completes before generation starts streaming.
FastAPI can expose streaming responses using Server-Sent Events.
The UI can display retrieval status before LLM token streaming begins.
topics.code:
async for chunk in chain.astream(input):
    yield chunk

# FastAPI concept
StreamingResponse(
    generator(),
    media_type="text/event-stream"
)

topics.title: Hybrid Search
theory: Dense embeddings capture semantic meaning.
Sparse search such as BM25 captures exact keywords.
Hybrid search combines dense and sparse retrieval.
Hybrid retrieval can improve retrieval coverage.
EnsembleRetriever can combine BM25Retriever and VectorStoreRetriever.
topics.code:
ensemble_retriever = EnsembleRetriever(
    retrievers=[bm25_retriever, vector_retriever],
    weights=[0.5, 0.5]
)

docs = ensemble_retriever.invoke(query)

topics.title: Reranking & Contextual Compression
theory: A retriever finds candidate documents.
A reranker re-scores candidate chunks for relevance.
Cross-encoder models can be used for reranking.
Cohere Rerank and HuggingFace CrossEncoder can be used for reranking.
ContextualCompressionRetriever can wrap a retriever and compress or rerank retrieved content.
Reranking improves precision after initial retrieval.

roadmap.title: LangGraph State & Production RAG
roadmap.goal: Use LangGraph for stateful workflows, retries, branching and self-correcting RAG.

topics.title: LangGraph State Graph
theory: LangGraph models stateful workflows as graphs.
A State Graph contains shared state and processing nodes.
Nodes represent individual processing steps.
Edges connect workflow steps.
Conditional edges support decision-based routing.
LangGraph supports workflows that require cycles and state.
topics.code:
State
  ↓
Retrieve Node
  ↓
Grade Documents Node
  ↓
Conditional Edge
  ├── Relevant → Generate
  └── Irrelevant → Rewrite Query
                         ↓
                      Retrieve

topics.title: Self-Correction RAG
theory: Agentic RAG can evaluate retrieved documents before generation.
If documents are irrelevant, the system can rewrite the query.
The rewritten query can trigger another retrieval attempt.
LangGraph is suitable for cyclic self-correction workflows.
Checkpointing can persist workflow state.
Human-in-the-loop workflows can use persisted state for approvals.

Grade Docs
   ↓

Yes    No
 ↓      ↓
Generate Rewrite Query
          ↓
       Retrieve

Use reranking to improve retrieval precision.
Store chat history in external databases such as Redis or PostgreSQL.
Use custom SDK calls for performance-critical or highly customized paths.
